sections.title: What does an AI automation consultant do?
sections.content:
An AI automation consultant identifies a business process where automation can create a measurable result, then connects the data, software and human decisions required to operate it. The work is not limited to selecting an AI model. It includes workflow design, API integration, safeguards, deployment and measurement.

For a small business, that usually means improving a process already happening every day: qualifying incoming leads, preparing customer replies, extracting information from documents, updating a CRM, producing reports or routing requests to the right person.

sections.title: AI automation use cases for small businesses
sections.content:
The strongest first use case has a clear trigger, repeated steps and an owner who can confirm whether the output is correct. Examples include form-to-CRM qualification, support triage with human handoff, invoice or document extraction, appointment follow-up, sales research and weekly operational reporting.

I use [n8n consulting and automation](/en/services/remote-n8n-automation-consultant) when a visual workflow is the right operational layer, custom APIs when an integration needs more control, and Next.js + Supabase when the team also needs an interface or internal application.

sections.title: From one bottleneck to a production workflow
sections.content:
We begin with the current process: inputs, decisions, tools, exceptions, volume and cost of failure. I define a small first release and the metric it should improve, then build and test it with controlled data before connecting production accounts.

The workflow includes the unglamorous parts that make automation useful: duplicate prevention, retries, timeout handling, action logs, alerts and a manual path when confidence is low. Once the first workflow is stable, we decide from evidence whether another process deserves automation.

sections.title: Human approval, security and responsible automation
sections.content:
AI should not independently send a sensitive message, change financial data or update a critical record simply because a model produced an answer. I keep explicit human approval for high-impact actions and define what the system may do automatically.

Credentials stay outside workflow exports, access follows least privilege, and stored data is limited to what the process needs. For customer-facing systems, the design includes escalation, traceability and a clear way for a person to take over.

sections.title: Proof from systems already in production
sections.content:
My [project portfolio](/en/projects) includes a Codeur opportunity-monitoring workflow with scoring and human review, FlowRemote job collection and qualification, visitor tracking with actionable alerts, and complete products combining Next.js, Supabase, APIs and automation.

These examples show the full delivery chain: collect a signal, structure it, apply business rules or AI, let a person approve when necessary, then record the outcome. The same architecture can be adapted to a small business without forcing an oversized platform.

sections.title: Why automate with N8N?
sections.content:
N8N is the most powerful open-source automation platform on the market. The project has over 90,000 stars on [GitHub](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n) and is used by thousands of companies worldwide.

Unlike Zapier or Make, N8N offers total control over your data (self-hosted), 400+ native integrations referenced in the [official library](https://n8n.io/integrations) and the ability to create complex logic with conditional branches, loops, sub-workflows and custom JavaScript or Python code inside nodes.

As an N8N expert in Madagascar, I design automations that run continuously, without human intervention, and scale with your business growth. The [official n8n documentation](https://docs.n8n.io) remains my daily reference to stay aligned with best practices.

sections.title: n8n vs Zapier vs Make: why I choose n8n
sections.content:
The automation platform you choose determines your monthly costs, your vendor dependency and the complexity of workflows you can build.

**Zapier** bills per executed task. With 100+ active zaps and a few thousand monthly operations, the bill quickly climbs to $250-$650 per month. Workflows remain simple (linear, limited conditional logic).

**Make** (formerly Integromat) offers more flexibility than Zapier but stays a proprietary service billed per operation. No self-hosting available.

**n8n** downloads for free and self-hosts on a $5-10 VPS regardless of execution volume. The official cloud version exists too for those who don't want to manage infrastructure. Workflows can embed custom JavaScript or Python code, connect to any REST or GraphQL API, and orchestrate AI agents through [LangChain](https://www.langchain.com).

For my European and US clients, n8n cuts the monthly automation bill by 5 to 10x compared to Zapier, with full workflow portability and zero vendor lock-in as a bonus.

faq.question: What is N8N exactly?
faq.answer: N8N is an open-source workflow automation platform. It connects your applications (Gmail, Slack, Airtable, Stripe, etc.) and creates automatic processes without coding. It's like Zapier, but more powerful with total control over your data.

faq.question: How much does an N8N workflow cost?

faq.question: Is my data secure?
faq.answer: Absolutely. N8N can be hosted on your own server (self-hosted), meaning your data never passes through third-party servers. I configure secure workflows with encryption and access control.

faq.question: Can N8N be combined with artificial intelligence?
faq.answer: Yes. I regularly integrate AI agents (Claude, GPT) into N8N workflows for text processing, automatic classification, content generation and data analysis. The native LangChain node in n8n lets you build multi-step agents with vector memory.

faq.question: How long does it take to deliver an n8n workflow?

faq.question: Which server should I host n8n on?
faq.answer: n8n runs on any Docker-capable VPS. My 2026 recommendations: Hetzner ($5/month, EU, GDPR-friendly), Render (free tier to start), or Railway ($5/month, one-click deploy). For heavier loads, an OVH or Scaleway VPS at $10-20/month easily handles thousands of executions per day.

sections.title: Prompt engineering for Claude Code
sections.content:
Claude Code is not magic: output quality depends on the context you provide. That's where prompt engineering becomes critical.

**CLAUDE.md at the repo root** — Reference document that Claude Code reads first. I include: tech stack, code conventions, architectural decisions, GDPR constraints, useful commands (test, lint, deploy). Without this file, Claude rediscovers everything every session and loses 20-40% of productivity.

**OODA-loop prompts** — Observe (read the context), Orient (understand why), Decide (propose a plan), Act (implement). I structure my prompts in this order so Claude doesn't skip the reasoning step.

**Subtask decomposition** — Instead of *"refactor the entire auth module"*, I split: *"list the files in the auth module"* → *"propose 3 ways to refactor session handling"* → *"implement option 2 while keeping backward compatibility"*. Every subtask is testable and reversible.

**Custom skills** — For repetitive workflows (new n8n project, SEO audit, landing generation), I create reusable Claude skills in `~/.claude/skills`. Productivity multiplied by 3 on recurring tasks.

sections.title: What is an AI agent, exactly?
sections.content:
An AI agent is a system that reasons, decides and then acts autonomously to reach a goal, using external tools such as an API, a database or the web. What sets it apart from a chatbot or a linear automation is decision autonomy: where a chatbot answers a question and an automation follows a fixed path, an agent assesses a situation, picks the right action, executes it, checks the result and corrects itself when needed.

In practice, an agent can read an incoming email, query your CRM, draft a reply, create a task and notify the right person, all without human input on standard cases. This reason, act, verify loop is what distinguishes a true agent from a scripted automation.

sections.title: Use cases that deliver real value
sections.content:
The most profitable AI agents handle repetitive tasks that require judgment, not just execution. Four families stand out.

The customer support agent qualifies requests, answers common questions using your documentation and escalates complex cases to a human. The prospecting agent enriches contacts, personalizes messages and organizes follow-up. The data and document processing agent extracts, classifies and structures information from invoices, PDFs or emails. Finally, the self-correcting autonomous workflow chains several steps, detects its own errors and retries whatever failed.

Every agent is designed around a measurable business goal, not around the technology itself.

sections.content:
I build AI agents on a proven stack: n8n for workflow orchestration, Claude Code for development, and large language model APIs (Claude, GPT) for reasoning. Connecting to your tools (CRM, email, database, web) turns the model into an agent that can actually act on your environment.

sections.title: Reliability, guardrails and going to production

An AI agent in production demands guardrails, otherwise autonomy becomes a liability. I treat reliability as an engineering concern in its own right, not as an afterthought.

Concretely: context management (the context window) so the agent keeps useful information without saturating, fallbacks to handle cases where the model hesitates or fails, and observability to trace every decision and action. Write-access limits on a production database are defined from the start, so an agent can never alter critical data without validation. This discipline lets you deploy autonomous agents while keeping control, which reassures both technical teams and management.

sections.title: What is this service called?
sections.content:
This is **technical optimization for an existing website**, also known as a website performance audit or cloud architecture optimization. It goes beyond a PageSpeed report: I investigate why the product consumes CPU, egress, serverless functions or database reads, then fix the system creating those costs.

It is useful when the product already works but pages are slowing down, free-tier quotas disappear unexpectedly, crawlers trigger expensive processing or every visit reloads the same data.

sections.title: What I actually audit
sections.content:
I start from verifiable symptoms: response times, network waterfalls, Core Web Vitals, Vercel logs, Supabase metrics, egress volume, function frequency, response size and SQL queries. I then connect every cost to the code path that triggers it.

The analysis covers Next.js rendering modes (static, dynamic and ISR), browser and CDN caching, calls to Payload or another CMS, data fallbacks, polling, images, server-side libraries and cache invalidation after publishing.

sections.title: The manda-ia.com case: data volume was not the problem
sections.content:
The database held about **25 MB**, yet the organization had exceeded **5.5 GB of egress**. The audit showed that public pages were dynamically rendered and fetched several remote sources on every request. Crawlers, visitors and refreshes repeatedly triggered the same work.

I replaced those reads with pre-rendered pages and revalidation, made the remote CMS opt-in in production, added shared caches, limited visitor dashboard polling to visible tabs and moved its cache to the Vercel edge. The dashboard stays less than 30 seconds behind without querying Supabase for every visitor.

sections.title: My four-step optimization method
sections.content:
**1. Measure** a baseline before changing anything. **2. Locate** the routes, requests and components responsible for usage. **3. Fix** the rendering mode, remove redundant reads, shrink responses and cache at the right layer. **4. Verify** the metrics, data freshness and user journeys to catch regressions.

I document both changes and trade-offs. Your team knows what was fixed, why it mattered and which metrics to keep watching.

sections.title: Deliverables, timeline and rate
sections.content:
You receive a prioritized diagnosis, a map of technical cost drivers, the agreed code changes, before-and-after measurements and guardrails to prevent the issue returning. A focused audit can take a few days; a full optimization depends on the number of routes, providers and data flows.

My standard rate is **EUR 350/day**, with scope and quote agreed before work starts. The engagement can stand alone or become part of continuous product improvement.

comparisonTable.title: Quick patch or structural optimization?
comparisonTable.intro: Both can improve a score in the short term, but only end-to-end analysis reduces infrastructure usage and risk sustainably.

comparisonTable.conclusion: The goal is not to cache everything. It is to recompute only what truly needs to change, when doing so creates value for the user.

faq.question: How is this different from a PageSpeed audit?
faq.answer: PageSpeed mainly evaluates loading experience in the browser. My audit also connects that experience to server costs: Next.js rendering, API calls, Vercel functions, Supabase egress, SQL queries, CMS reads and caching strategy.

faq.question: Can you optimize a live website without rebuilding it?
faq.answer: Yes. I start with high-impact, low-risk changes and expand only when the architecture requires it. The purpose is to improve the existing product, not force an unnecessary rebuild.

faq.question: Do you only work with Vercel and Supabase?
faq.answer: No. This case uses Vercel, Supabase, Next.js and Payload, but the method applies to other hosts, databases, CMS platforms and APIs. Tools vary; measurement, caching and request-reduction principles remain the same.

faq.question: Can caching show stale data?
faq.answer: A well-designed cache has an appropriate lifetime and invalidation strategy. Editorial pages can revalidate after publishing; a near-real-time dashboard can use a shared 30-second cache. Freshness is selected according to the business requirement.

faq.question: What results should I expect?
faq.answer: Results depend on traffic and architecture. The measurable targets are fewer requests and transfers, lighter responses, faster loading and more headroom before quotas. I provide before-and-after values instead of a generic promise.

items.title: International Opportunity Agent
items.subtitle: RSS monitoring, AI qualification and human-approved outreach
items.description: An assisted prospecting system built to detect relevant international contracts without turning applications into blind automated outreach. Every 60 minutes, n8n reads four public RSS sources, normalizes listings and deduplicates them in PostgreSQL. New opportunities are scored with deterministic business rules, then analyzed through OpenRouter when they reach the useful threshold. The strongest matches arrive in Gmail with a concise brief, a tailored draft and two expiring links: approve or reject. An application can only be sent after human approval and only when the public listing explicitly contains a contact email. Everything else remains a manual application. The workflow includes an AI fallback model, retry paths, a decision history and a delivery record for every Gmail send.

about.bio: I'm Mandaniaina Randriambinintsoa, freelance developer based in Antananarivo. Trained in Computer Science (Master's, ESTI), I started with JavaScript development. In 2023 I moved to No-Code, Bubble and Webflow, because it let me ship working products in a few weeks. That worked well for three years. Late 2025, AI-assisted development changed the game. I went back to pure code, because code is still the most flexible option when you need to configure servers, build real architecture and handle scale.
